eligibility.reason: The primary issue identifies controller acceleration settings newly effective in Jazzy, not an odometry format, frame, unit or timing violation by a named peer. A controller compared across distributions with its own unchanged parameter file is not by itself two separately deployed units in an UPGRADE. Under the specification's candidate odometry/controller composition, E2 stops at internal. The later open-loop enhancement concerns another tested robot and does not prove the original issue had a different inter-unit cause.
eligibility.quote: and it is effective in JAZZY. It seems that the small acceleration value causes the vehicle to slow down.

loudness.quote: I had to increase ax_max to 15.0 in order to make my robot move as fast as I wanted, which I feel doesn’t make much sense.
loudness.reason: Not applicable after exclusion. The report is about achieved motion, not a documented interface diagnostic.

detection_stage.quote: It seems that the small acceleration value causes the vehicle to slow down.
detection_stage.reason: The source describes runtime behavior; the excluded-case field remains null.

resolution.quote: We saw the same symptom class as #5386 and #5694 (that one reported 0.17 m/s and we similarly measured 0.173)
resolution.reason: Null means excluded, not unimplemented. The later Ridgeback simulation is explicitly the same symptom class, not the original composition with both units pinned.

notes: Read the original report excerpt and all returned issue comments, PRs 5617 and 6336, and 6336's optimizer.cpp diff. The specification's E1 says the backport merged in 2025, but the opened API https://api.github.com/repos/ros-navigation/navigation2/pulls/6336 reports merged_at as '2026-08-11T18:35:27Z', agreeing with its notes rather than its E1 date.
